title: Reactor typeface, FUSE poster
lede: Tobias Frere-Jones’s distressed sans-serif for the experimental type magazine FUSE, shown on its FUSE poster as white capitals that break up line by line.
summary: White eroded capitals on a black, smeared photographic ground, with a yellow line at the foot. Tobias Frere-Jones, FUSE, 1993.
made: 1993 (Fonts In Use; poster credit line); released by Font Bureau in 1996

evidence.note: Inspected the FUSE poster for Reactor as reproduced in Typographica’s review of the FUSE 1–20 book (1647 × 2340), and the Fonts In Use type sample (856 × 194), in scratchpad copies. The FUSE issue number was not confirmed. Not stored.

styles.note: Clear example: a font drawn damaged, whose distress grows as more text is set.

context: Fonts In Use says Frere-Jones designed Reactor in 1993 for Neville Brody and Jon Wozencroft’s FUSE; Font Bureau released it in 1996, and it is no longer sold. [Fonts In Use](https://fontsinuse.com/typefaces/26615/fb-reactor).

Chris Hamamoto describes Reactor as “inspired by a burning building and its ruins”, with lowercase letters that contain copies of other characters extending into their neighbours, adding distress “the more type is set”. [Typographica](https://typographica.org/typography-books/fuse-1-20/).

Wikipedia’s list of Frere-Jones typefaces calls Reactor (1993–96) “an example of the ‘grunge typography’ style of the 1990s”, citing Ellen Lupton. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_typefaces_designed_by_Tobias_Frere-Jones).
observed: The poster is black with a grey, smeared photographic texture in the upper half and a dark photograph of machinery or wreckage at the foot.

Five lines of white capitals, cropped at both page edges, read like an incident report: “…WER LOSS IN ENGINE 3”, “…TIONAL DOWN 95 POI…”, “…ORE INTEGRITY SUSP…”, “…RNAL STRUCTURE DAM…”, “…LTIPLE SKULL FRACTU…”.
The first line is only lightly rough; each following line has more specks, torn edges, and stray fragments, until the letters in the last line are hard to separate.
A final line, “I CAN HEAR IT NOW”, is set in yellow in the same face with little damage.
The small credit line reads “F REACTOR ® 1993 FONTSHOP INTERNATIONAL © 1993 TOBIAS FRERE-JONES” in a plain monospaced face.
In the Fonts In Use sample, the capitals are a narrow humanist sans-serif with ragged, splintered edges and doubled strokes.
interpretation: Reactor makes distress a function of the text, not a filter: the more you type, the worse it gets. The poster shows the style’s link between damage and content.
borrow: Increase distress down a stack of display lines, so the page seems to decay as it is read.
Crop display lines at both edges of the page, as if the text continues off-screen.

rights.statement: No image is stored. © 1993 Tobias Frere-Jones and FontShop International, per the poster’s credit line.
